lessons.title: Collections and efficient lookup
lessons.subtitle: None then ['a'] before modification; ['a', 'c'] after.
lessons.concept: A list preserves order, a set removes duplicates, and a dictionary maps keys to values. Building an index takes one pass over the products; subsequent ID lookups take constant time on average. Duplicate IDs overwrite an entry, so explicitly decide to reject them.

explanation.text: A list preserves order, a set removes duplicates, and a dictionary maps keys to values. Building an index takes one pass over the products; subsequent ID lookups take constant time on average. Duplicate IDs overwrite an entry, so explicitly decide to reject them.

exercise.task: Add an in-stock product c, then verify that two a IDs are rejected.
hints: An index does not detect duplicates by itself. The key in result check protects the contract.

lessons.title: Import CSV without losing errors
lessons.subtitle: One accepted row and one error on line 3; two of each after modification.
lessons.concept: A CSV file contains text, even in numeric columns. DictReader uses headers as keys. Validate each row and keep its line number with any error so it can be corrected. Separate accepted and rejected data; an error must not silently remove an order.

explanation.text: A CSV file contains text, even in numeric columns. DictReader uses headers as keys. Validate each row and keep its line number with any error so it can be corrected. Separate accepted and rejected data; an error must not silently remove an order.

explanation.title: Expected result
explanation.text: One accepted row and one error on line 3; two of each after modification.

exercise.task: Add c,-1 and d,0 rows. Verify that zero is accepted but -1 is not.
hints: One accepted row and one error on line 3; two of each after modification.
An overly broad except can hide a bug. Catch expected data errors here and let other errors propagate.
exercise.solution:
accepted, errors = parse_catalog("sku,stock
a,3
b,no
c,-1
d,0
")
assert accepted == [{"sku": "a", "stock": 3}, {"sku": "d", "stock": 0}]
assert [e["line"] for e in errors] == [3, 4]

lessons.title: Models and invariants
lessons.subtitle: 3; a rejected reservation does not change stock.
lessons.concept: A dataclass groups an object’s data. An invariant is a rule that must always hold: stock never becomes negative. The reserve method centralizes this rule instead of copying it into every screen. This in-memory model teaches the rule; real shared inventory also needs a database transaction.
